Summary  
Data source overview: The blog-style post is a personal 2017 year-in-review that briefly references two technical AI-safety publications (“RL with Reward Corruption” and “AI Safety Gridworlds”) and an interpretability talk. Although the post provides only headlines, each reference implicitly points to well-known safety problems (reward corruption and model opacity) together with the authors’ empirical grid-world experiments and interpretability demonstrations.  

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[73]  
Instruction-set improvement: The current instruction set assumes that every data source will explicitly contain detailed causal chains. When sources only mention papers/talks, it would help to add an explicit clause clarifying the level of acceptable moderate inference and encouraging the extractor to look up abstracts if citations are provided. Clearer guidance on edge direction conventions (e.g., always from higher-level problem toward solution) would also reduce ambiguity.  

Inference strategy justification: The post does not supply methodological detail, so moderate inference (edge confidence=2) was used based on common knowledge of the cited work. Each inferred statement is anchored to the closest bullet/section that mentions the work, satisfying traceability.  

Extraction completeness explanation: All safety-relevant material in the post centres on the two cited publications and the interpretability talk. Both causal fabrics are fully expanded from risk → … → intervention and interconnected via shared design-level nodes, leaving no isolated components.  

Key limitations:  
1. The source lacks experimental numbers, so validation evidence nodes are paraphrased from well-known results rather than directly quoted.  
2. Intervention details are necessarily high-level; real implementations would need finer granularity.  
3. Some cross-connections may be speculative because the blog post does not spell them out.
